claims.text: Refractory multi-principal-element alloys can suffer room-temperature brittleness because aging produces intrinsically brittle secondary phases such as silicides, B2, and Laves phases.
A multistage thermo-mechanical and stepwise aging route can produce a simultaneous strength-ductility improvement in a W-Ni-Fe-Ta multi-principal-element alloy.
The proposed route generates two distinct coherent nanoprecipitate phases in a stepwise and independently controllable manner.
The two coherent precipitates have different lattice parameters and phase-transition temperatures.
The relevant W-Ni-Fe-Ta alloy begins from a supersaturated solid-solution matrix suitable for precipitation.
Traditional single-principal-element W alloys containing brittle W-enriched bcc phases exhibit a difficult strength-ductility trade-off.
The demonstrated processing sequence consists of homogenization, hot rolling, cold rolling, annealing near 900 °C, aging near 650 °C, and quenching.
Processing in argon prevents oxidation of the alloy.
The high-temperature step allows the first precipitate to form and stabilize before the lower-temperature step nucleates the second precipitate.
Water quenching retains the desired nanoscale precipitate distribution.
The SCCP microstructure contains coherent Ni3Ta-based δ lamellas with a D0a structure.
The SCCP microstructure also contains coherent γ″ particles with a D022 structure.
High lattice friction and precipitation hardening specifically associated with the coherent δ lamellas provide ultrahigh yield strength.
Dislocation interactions with hierarchical γ″ particles and coherent interfaces produce progressive multistage strain hardening.
Progressive multistage strain hardening prevents premature strain localization and thereby preserves tensile ductility.
The stepwise-processed alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength exceeding 2000 MPa.
The stepwise-processed alloy will have at least 15% uniform tensile ductility at room temperature.
The alloy will retain a yield strength above 1000 MPa at 800 °C.
The alloy will retain significant tensile ductility at 800 °C.
The applicable alloy matrix is a body-centered-cubic solid solution capable of forming coherent D0a and D022 intermetallic precipitates.

contradictions.description: The predicted uniform ductility is at least 15%, but the falsification rule accepts any ductility above 10%; an outcome between 10% and 15% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The target is described as a multi-principal-element alloy, while the initial state is alternatively described as containing a single principal element or dilute additions; these are materially different alloy-design regimes and are not clearly separated.
